concepts.def: Strikes and bread queues in Petrograd, joined by mutinying soldiers, forced Tsar Nicholas II to abdicate in March 1917.
The Bolsheviks, organised by Trotsky and led by Lenin, seized key points in Petrograd and overthrew the Provisional Government.
The Reds defended the revolution against the Whites and foreign intervention; Trotsky's Red Army and control of the centre secured Bolshevik victory.
Lenin's retreat from War Communism, allowing peasants to sell surplus grain and small businesses to trade, after famine and the Kronstadt rising.
From 1928 Stalin merged peasant farms into collective farms (kolkhozy) to control grain; 'kulaks' were deported and famine struck in 1932-33.
Stalin's purges of the 1930s: show trials of Old Bolsheviks, mass NKVD arrests, the Gulag camps, and the decimation of the Red Army officer corps.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Russia & the Soviet Union 1917-41 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Russia & the Soviet Union 1917-41 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Russia & the Soviet Union 1917-41.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who organised and led the Red Army during the Civil War?
options: Trotsky
Stalin
Kerensky
Kamenev

mcqs.q: Why did Lenin introduce the New Economic Policy in 1921?
options: To revive the economy after War Communism had caused famine and revolts such as Kronstadt
To prepare Russia for war with Germany
To hand the economy over to foreign companies
To abolish money throughout Russia
Collective farms created under Stalin
Secret police units
Factories built under the Five-Year Plans
Councils of soldiers and workers

mcqs.q: What happened at the Moscow show trials of 1936-38?
options: Leading Old Bolsheviks confessed to fabricated crimes and most were executed
Stalin himself was put on trial by the party
Tsarist generals were tried for the First World War
Foreign diplomats were tried for espionage and acquitted

mcqs.q: Was the October Revolution a huge popular battle?
options: No - it was a planned seizure of key points by relatively small Bolshevik forces, and the Winter Palace fell with little fighting, though the Bolsheviks had real support in the soviets.
The October Revolution took place mainly in Moscow.
Stalin was elected leader by a national vote of the Soviet people.
Thousands died storming the Winter Palace in a massive battle.

mcqs.q: Did Lenin choose Stalin as his successor?
options: No - Lenin's Testament criticised Stalin and suggested removing him as General Secretary; Stalin outmanoeuvred rivals like Trotsky in the power struggle of 1924-29.
Stalin was elected leader by a national vote of the Soviet people.
Stalin was Lenin's chosen and announced heir.
Collectivisation gave each peasant family its own private farm.

mcqs.q: Did collectivisation quickly increase food production?
options: Collectivisation gave each peasant family its own private farm.
No - peasants slaughtered livestock in protest, output fell, and state grain seizures contributed to the devastating famine of 1932-33, especially in Ukraine.
Collectivisation immediately modernised farming and ended hunger.
Stalin was elected leader by a national vote of the Soviet people.
